headline: S&P 500 fell 3.7% Friday (Nasdaq -5.3%, Dow -950 pts), a seventh straight loss; Dow and S&P are in correction after the worst week since April 2025 on AI fears, Nvidia turmoil and a 92%-priced December Fed hike. Futures rebound about 2% Sunday night. Short week: PCE Wednesday, closed Thursday.

sectors.why: No clear sector news. A December Fed hike is about 92% priced, a mild headwind, but nothing points one way.
No clear US telecom news. Telecoms held up better than tech in Friday's sell-off, but a hawkish Fed weighs on dividend stocks.

Futures price a December Fed hike (about 92%) and two or more hikes by June above 80%, which weighs on homes, cars and furniture. Fortune cites Moody's that the stock-market wealth effect may now slow growth.
Consumer staples was the only S&P sector to gain on Friday, so it may keep acting as a hiding place, but higher rates and soft spending limit upside.
No clear sector news. Thanksgiving week and Black Friday will show how spending holds up after the stock slump.
No clear sector news.

Chips led a 5.3% Nasdaq plunge Friday (NVDA -14%, AMD -13%, MU over -12%) on AI-spending doubts, Nvidia's CEO exit and SEC probe, and China chip-export worries. Futures bounce about 2.7% Monday, but trust is shaken.
WTI settled near $83, its lowest since late August, with Brent near $92 amid surplus talk. No clear one-month push either way.
Banks fell Friday (JPM and BAC over -3%, C -4%) as the S&P 500 entered a correction, and JPMorgan had a tech outage. Rate-hike fears and AI-financing worries weigh.
CMS proposed on 16 Nov to extrapolate Medicare Advantage audit findings back to 2018 (about $9B a year). UNH fell 10% and HUM 13% on 18 Nov; comments run to 19 Jan 2027, so the overhang stays.
No clear sector news for drug and device makers. Medtronic reports Tuesday.
Political pushback on data centers after the midterms (new governors pledging to halt construction) and Trump's vow to stop US firms building data centers abroad cloud AI-building demand.
No clear sector news.
Gold moves were reported in opposite directions by two sources on Friday, so there is no clear signal.
No clear sector news.
Deere reports Wednesday. Slower AI spending could hit power and equipment suppliers (Bloom Energy -15% Friday), but no clear one-month direction for the sector.
Big retail earnings Tuesday (Best Buy, Dollar Tree, Dick's, Burlington) and Black Friday this week. Results could move stocks either way.

AI stocks had their worst week since 2020: Anthropic fell 9% in its second session, neoclouds NBIS -16% and CRWV -12%. Futures rebound Monday, but AI-financing doubts and a hawkish Fed remain. Workday and Autodesk report Tuesday.
No clear sector news. United Airlines had a reported tech outage; lower oil helps costs.
Utilities could hold up in a sell-off, but data-center pushback may cut expected power demand growth. No clear direction.

avoid.NVDA: CEO Jensen Huang resigned, the SEC is probing whether disclosures misled investors, and leadership faces a congressional interview on 1 Dec.
avoid.HUM: Most exposed to the proposed CMS Medicare Advantage audit rule (fell 13% on 18 Nov); comment period runs to 19 Jan 2027.
avoid.UNH: Fell about 14% in a week on the CMS Medicare Advantage audit proposal; the overhang lasts until the rule is settled.
